Solitude to Triumph Friday, November 20, 2026: 7:30 PM Saturday, November 21, 2026: 2:30 PM Saturday, November 21, 2026: 7:30 PM Sunday, November 22, 2026: 2:30 PM Join us 45-minutes before each concert for a free pre-concert lecture with Brian DeMaris. All four concerts at the Gardner Theatre within Lancaster Country Day School 725 Hamilton Road, Lancaster, PA 17603 Concert Timing (approx.): 2 Hours (including a 20-minute intermission) Tickets: $25-$105 Experience a powerful emotional journey as we present three deeply lyrical masterworks. Copland's Quiet City evokes urban solitude and contemplation, while Barber's Violin Concerto—performed by Sphinx Competition winner Amaryn Olmeda—offers pensive, elegant songfulness that moves from introspection to brilliant virtuosity. The concert culminates with Sibelius' triumphant Symphony No. 2, building from reflection to a glorious, uplifting finale. From quiet contemplation to radiant celebration, this program reveals the full range of the human spirit through three profoundly beautiful works. Messiah By Candlelight Thursday, December 3, 2026: 7:00 PM Friday, December 4, 2026: 7:30 PM Saturday, December 5, 2026: 2:30 PM Saturday, December 5, 2026: 7:30 PM All four concerts at First Presbyterian Church of Lancaster 140 East Orange Street, Lancaster, PA 17602 Concert Timing (approx.): 2 Hours 30 Minutes (including a 20-minute intermission) Tickets: $45-$105 The Lancaster Symphony Orchestra and Chorus return to First Presbyterian Church of Lancaster for the 5th annual performance of Handel's Messiah—this year with a special twist. Experience this beloved masterwork performed entirely by candlelight, as flickering flames illuminate the music and the darkness deepens every note. From "Comfort Ye" to the triumphant "Hallelujah" Chorus, Messiah by Candlelight offers an intimate and unforgettable celebration of this timeless holiday tradition. In the warm acoustics of First Presbyterian Church, with orchestra, chorus, and soloists united by the glow of candlelight, this performance invites you to experience Handel's greatest work in a whole new light. events.description: For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440. Tales & Legends Friday, January 15, 2027: 7:30 PM Saturday, January 16, 2027: 2:30 PM Saturday, January 16, 2027: 7:30 PM Sunday, January 17, 2027: 2:30 PM Join us 45-minutes before each concert for a free pre-concert lecture with Chelsea Gallo. All four concerts at the Gardner Theatre within Lancaster Country Day School 725 Hamilton Road, Lancaster, PA 17603 Concert Timing (approx.): 2 Hours (including a 20-minute intermission) Tickets: $25-$105 Music's greatest storytellers take center stage in a program dedicated to the art of musical narrative. Wagner's grand Prelude to Die Meistersinger opens with themes of mastery and tradition, followed by the world premiere of Austin Wintory's Interactive Concerto for Guitar featuring 4-time Grammy-nominated guitarist Mak Grgic in an innovative new work that bridges classical and contemporary worlds. The concert concludes with Rimsky-Korsakov's enchanting Scheherazade—the ultimate musical storyteller—spinning tales from the Arabian Nights with exotic melodies, shimmering orchestration, and the seductive voice of the solo violin. From European legends to interactive innovation to Arabian tales, this concert celebrates music's timeless power to tell extraordinary stories. FEATURING: Chelsea Gallo, guest conductor Mak Grgic, guitarist REPERTOIRE: Richard Wagner: Prelude to Die MeistersingerAustin Wintory: Interactive Concerto for Guitar (World Premiere) Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov: Sheherazade, op.35 For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440.

Triple Concerto Friday, March 12, 2027: 7:30 PM Saturday, March 13, 2027: 2:30 PM Saturday, March 13, 2027: 7:30 PM Sunday, March 14, 2027: 2:30 PM Join us 45-minutes before each concert for a free pre-concert lecture with Na’Zir McFadden. All four concerts at the Gardner Theatre within Lancaster Country Day School 725 Hamilton Road, Lancaster, PA 17603 Concert Timing (approx.): 2 Hours (including a 20-minute intermission) Tickets: $25-$105 Witness a rare orchestral treasure as three world-class soloists unite for Beethoven's Triple Concerto—violinist Jennifer Frautschi, cellist Zuill Bailey, and pianist Christopher Shih—in an extraordinary conversation between three virtuosos and orchestra. The program opens with Tina Davidson's Bright Air, Brilliant Fire, inspired by ancient philosophy's four elements, and continues with Mendelssohn's beloved "Italian" Symphony, described by the composer as "blue sky in A major" and brimming with Mediterranean sunshine and dance. From elemental fire and Italian light to Beethoven's remarkable three-way dialogue, this concert showcases brilliant soloists in an unforgettable celebration of chamber music on the grandest scale. events.title: Beethoven 9
events.description: For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440. Beethoven 9 Friday, May 7, 2027: 7:30 PM Saturday, May 8, 2027: 2:30 PM Saturday, May 8, 2027: 7:30 PM Sunday, May 9, 2027: 2:30 PM Join us 45-minutes before each concert for a free pre-concert lecture with Morihiko Nakahara. All four concerts at the Gardner Theatre within Lancaster Country Day School 725 Hamilton Road, Lancaster, PA 17603 Concert Timing (approx.): 2 Hours (including a 20-minute intermission) Tickets: $25-$105 Join us as we crown our 80th Anniversary Season with one of music's most monumental achievements: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony. This historic finale features the regional premiere of Jeffrey Nytch's powerful Hunger Stones—a contemplative work inspired by ancient climate warnings carved into European riverbeds—and Brahms' joyful Academic Festival Overture, a rousing potpourri of student songs. The evening culminates with Beethoven's revolutionary Ninth Symphony, uniting orchestra, chorus, and vocal soloists in the transcendent "Ode to Joy"—a triumphant celebration of humanity's highest aspirations. From ancient warnings to eternal joy, this season finale honors 80 years of the Lancaster Symphony Orchestra bringing music and community together. FEATURING: Morihiko Nakahara, guest conductorLancaster Symphony Chorus Dr. William Wright, chorusmaster REPERTOIRE: Nytch: Hunger Stones (Regional Premiere) Johannes Brahms: Academic Festival Overture, op.80 Ludwig van Beethoven: Symphony No. 9 in D minor, op.125 For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440.
